recursion_runtime.title: Hands-on: Implement and Measure foo
recursion_runtime.prompt:
Open `algorithms/recursion.c`. Implement the two recursive branches, then run the supplied harness. Work in this order:

1. Confirm the base case `i == n`.
2. Set `bits[i] = true` and recurse with `i + 1`.
3. Return to the same frame, set `bits[i] = false`, and recurse again.
4. Check `n = 0`, `1`, `3`, and `4` against the call-tree formulas.

The validator checks observable counts. Equivalent correct implementations pass; branch order, helper names, formatting, and literal source phrases are not graded.
recursion_runtime.hint: For a call with `m = n - i` undecided positions: the base case has one call and one leaf; otherwise the current call contributes one plus the two subtrees for `m - 1`.

help.concept: Every internal call represents one partial Boolean prefix. Its true and false children extend that prefix by one position. Therefore `leaves = 2^n` and `calls = 1 + 2 + ... + 2^n = 2^(n+1) - 1`.
help.hint_1: Increment `calls` once, immediately when the helper starts.
help.hint_2: After the true recursive call returns, overwrite only `bits[i]` with false; earlier prefix values stay unchanged.

checks.message: Run the provided behavioral harness and use the failing case to locate the logic error.
Equivalent correct implementations are accepted; no exact source phrase is required.

recurrence.title: Which recurrence matches fooRec when printing a completed list is O(1)?
recurrence.prompt: Which recurrence matches fooRec when printing a completed list is O(1)?
recurrence.hint: One non-base call does constant local work and creates two calls with one fewer undecided position.

help.concept: Define `T(m)` using the number of positions still undecided. Then both children have size `m - 1`.
help.hint_1: Count recursive calls, not assignments: there are two recursive calls.
help.hint_2: The assignments, comparison, counter update, and return are constant local work.

tight-bound.title: What tight bound follows after unrolling the recurrence?
tight-bound.prompt: What tight bound follows after unrolling the recurrence?
tight-bound.hint: Unroll until the argument reaches zero; the constants form `1 + 2 + 4 + ...`.

help.concept: After `k` substitutions, `T(n) = 2^k T(n-k) + c(2^k - 1)`. Set `k = n` to reach `T(0)`.
help.hint_1: Do not replace the geometric sum by `n`; its terms double.
help.hint_2: Both the base-case term and accumulated local work are proportional to `2^n`.

introduction.title: Read → Watch → Build → Explain
introduction.bodyMarkdown:
### How to work through this CS260 assignment course

This draft follows **CS260 Written Assignment 2 (Summer 2024–25)** and uses the same answer discipline expected by the assignment:

1. State the algorithm in clear C/Python-like pseudocode or C.
2. Explain the high-level idea in plain English.
3. Trace one concrete input by hand before claiming correctness.
4. Explain why every step preserves the required property.
5. Count the real work and give the requested asymptotic bound.

Every lesson uses the same rhythm: **read the exact problem → trace actual values → watch the data/call structure change → implement → explain correctness → analyze runtime**.

Recursive algorithms are drawn as **call trees**. Each node is one real function call, each edge is one recursive branch, and the active path follows the depth-first execution order. Iterative algorithms show loop indices, stack contents, table entries, or pointer positions after every important operation.

The coding labs grade observable behavior. Equivalent correct solutions pass even when they use different helper names, loop forms, safe table sizes, midpoint choices, or node-reuse strategies. Exact source phrases are never the requirement.

question-1-problem.title: Question 1: Read the Function and the Runtime Goal

recursion-animation.title: Trace foo(3) as a Call Tree, Then Solve T(n)
recursion-animation.context: **Board-style trace:** execute the actual `fooRec(L,3,0)` control flow, reveal the complete call tree in depth-first order, count each level, and then substitute the matching recurrence one algebra line at a time.

steps.title: Start with the root call
steps.body: `foo(3)` allocates three Boolean positions and enters `foo_rec(bits, 3, 0, &stats)`. The root owns position `0`; no branch has been chosen yet.

steps.title: One call creates two children
steps.body: At `i = 0`, the function first assigns `true` and calls `i = 1`. After that entire subtree returns, the same frame assigns `false` and calls `i = 1` again.

steps.title: Follow the first depth-first path
steps.body: The first recursive call keeps choosing `true`: `T__ → TT_ → TTT`. Entering `i = 3` increments `calls` to `4`; because `i == n`, this is the first leaf.

steps.title: Backtrack to produce TTF
steps.body: Returning from `TTT` restores the `i = 2` stack frame. That frame changes only `bits[2]` to `false`, producing `TTF`. The prefix `TT` stays fixed because it belongs to earlier frames.

steps.title: Finish the entire true-prefix subtree
steps.body: After `TTT` and `TTF`, control returns to `i = 1`, changes `bits[1]` to false, and generates `TFT` and `TFF`. The left half of the call tree is now complete.

steps.title: Complete foo(3)
steps.body: The root then explores the false-prefix subtree and produces `FTT, FTF, FFT, FFF`. There are eight leaves because each of three positions has two choices.

steps.title: Count calls one tree level at a time
steps.body: For `n = 3`, level `j` contains `2^j` calls. The base cases are at level `3`, so there are `2^3 = 8` leaves. Summing all levels gives `1+2+4+8=15` total calls. This picture is the concrete reason the recurrence accumulates a geometric series.

steps.title: Translate the call tree into a recurrence
steps.body: Let `T(n)` mean `n` undecided positions. One call performs constant local work `c` and creates two size-`n-1` calls. The base case performs constant work `d`.

steps.title: Substitute once and distribute the 2
steps.body: Replace `T(n-1)` with `2T(n-2)+c`. The outside factor `2` multiplies both terms, and the original final `+c` remains.

steps.title: Substitute again and recognize the pattern
steps.body: One more substitution produces eight subproblems and seven copies of the constant work. The coefficients `1, 3, 7, 15, ...` are one less than powers of two.

steps.title: Write the result after k substitutions
steps.body: After `k` levels, there are `2^k` remaining subproblems. The accumulated local work is a geometric series.

steps.title: Reach the base case
steps.body: Set `n-k=0`, so `k=n`. Substitute the base cost `T(0)=d` and simplify.

steps.title: State the tight bound and stack space
steps.body: The tree has `2^n` leaves and `2^(n+1)-1` total calls, so the running time is `Θ(2^n)`. Only one root-to-leaf path is active at a time, so recursion-stack space is `Θ(n)`.
